title: APO White Turkey Meatballs with Ginger-Lime Gravy
description: White turkey meatballs stay soft with a milk panade and covered steam, then get a glossy ginger-lime and sesame gravy.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe, bottom drip pan and middle wire rack

ingredients.name: plain ground turkey breast
ingredients.note: White meat only, no added brine or seasoning.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water without a vegetable seasoning blend.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Squeeze grated ginger and discard fibers.

ingredients.name: hot water
ingredients.note: Keep ready for adjusting liquid depth or sauce yield; use only as needed.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 275°F with sous vide mode off, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 165°F.

steps.title: Soften the crumbs
steps.text: Soak {crumbs} in {milk} for 5 minutes until fully soft.

steps.title: Mix the meatballs
steps.text: Stir {egg} and {garlic} into the panade. Gently fold in {turkey} just until combined.

steps.title: Portion into the pan
steps.text: Form three equal meatballs per serving. Arrange in a snug deep oven dish with a shallow layer of {broth}, reserving the remaining clean broth for gravy.

steps.title: Probe and cover
steps.text: Insert the probe sideways into the center of the largest ball without touching the pan. Cover the dish with foil and place on the middle rack. Begin cooking immediately and set a separate 18-minute reminder for the first temperature check; respond sooner if the probe signals.

steps.title: Simmer the ginger base
steps.text: While the meatballs cook, simmer the reserved {broth}, {ginger}, {aminos} and {honey} in the HexClad for 3 minutes. Add a splash of {topup} if needed to yield about 3/8 cup of sauce base per serving.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Add lime and sesame
steps.text: Whisk {lime} and {sesame} into the gravy off heat.

steps.title: Steam the meatballs
steps.text: Cook covered for 20–38 minutes until the probe reads 165°F. Verify 165°F in several other large centers before lifting the dish from the oven. Leave the meatballs covered in their liquid.

steps.title: Coat all the meatballs
steps.text: Transfer the cooked meatballs to the skillet, roll them gently in gravy and divide the remaining gravy among the bowls.

notes: Make ahead: Shape the meatballs up to a day ahead and refrigerate covered. Add the broth just before cooking. Option A uses lime and ginger. For gentler Option B, omit the lime and halve the ginger. Plain unsweetened oat milk can replace milk in the panade. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze several meatballs together in enough gravy to cover them for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: Place one portion and its sauce in a shallow covered dish. Install the APO bottom drip pan and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Insert the probe in the coldest center and set it to 165°F. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw a single portion in the refrigerator overnight, then use the fridge reheating method. Stir the sauce until smooth.
